binderhub/build.py:146-171 Build.get_cmd constructs the jupyter-repo2docker command list from self.ref, self.image_name, self.appendix, self.repo_url

binderhub/build.py:327-373 Build.submit creates the build pod: client.V1Container(image=..., args=self.get_cmd(), env=[client.V1EnvVar(name='GIT_CREDENTIAL_ENV', value=self.git_credentials)]) inside client.V1Pod, then api.create_namespaced_pod (line 376)
binderhub/builder.py:397-422 BuildHandler builds appendix via self.settings['appendix'].format(repo_url=..., ref_url=...) and passes repo_url/ref/image_name into BuildClass
binderhub/builder.py:424-430 build_pool.submit(build.submit) dispatches pod creation onto a worker pool
binderhub/builder.py:590-594 launcher.launch(...) forwards image/repo_url to JupyterHub REST API (binderhub/launcher.py:149-250) - network API, not a local command execution

notes: Extraction rules were derived only from repo evidence and the CWE-78 pass focus; no vulnerability ground truth, fix commits, or vulnerability descriptions were consulted.
subprocess.run in repoproviders.py:488 is list-form (no shell); it is extracted as a candidate for argument injection (CWE-78 family) without any assumption that it is vulnerable.
Keyword-position sinks are encoded in the callable column as '<Constructor>.<keyword>' (e.g. 'V1Container.args') with arg_index -1; positional sinks use the concrete positional arg_index.
